@graph.name: Baked Chicken Breast Recipe
@graph.description: These easy Baked Chicken Breasts are marinated in a simple brine before being seasoned to perfection and baked in the oven until golden, tender, and JUICY!
recipeIngredient: 1 Tbsp granulated sugar (optional, (can omit for keto/low-carb) $0.02**)
½ tsp brown sugar (optional (omit for sugar-free/keto) $0.01**)

recipeInstructions.text: Place the chicken breasts between sheets of plastic wrap or put them inside a gallon-size baggie. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin to pound the thicker ends until each breast is an even ½- to ¾-inch thickness throughout.
recipeInstructions.name: Pound the chicken

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, add the pounded chicken, 2 quarts of cold water, 2 Tbsp kosher salt, and 1 Tbsp granulated sugar. You can also brine the chicken breasts in a Gallon size (maybe 2) zip-top bag.
recipeInstructions.name: Make the brine

recipeInstructions.text: Cover and refrigerate the submerged chicken breasts in the brine for 30 minutes. Do not exceed 45 minutes to prevent the meat texture from breaking down.
recipeInstructions.name: Brine the chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat your oven to 425°F. In a small bowl, combine the smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, black pepper, and brown sugar (if using).
recipeInstructions.name: Preheat and mix

recipeInstructions.text: Remove chicken from the brine, rinse quickly under cold water, and thoroughly pat completely dry with clean paper towels.*** Drizzle the breasts with olive oil, then rub the spice mix evenly over all sides of the chicken.
recipeInstructions.name: Season the chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Arrange seasoned chicken breasts in a single layer in a 9x13-inch baking dish or rimmed baking sheet. Bake uncovered at 425°F for 18-20 minutes, or until an instant-read thermometer registers 160-165°F in the thickest part of each chicken breast.
recipeInstructions.name: Bake the chicken breasts

recipeInstructions.text: Transfer chicken to a cutting board or plate, loosely tent with aluminum foil, and let rest for 5-10 minutes before cutting. The residual heat will finish bringing the internal temperature to 165°F while locking in all the juices. (see notes)
recipeInstructions.name: Rest and serve

review.reviewBody: I love chicken and eat a lot of it for the easy protein.  The brine really helped my chicken breasts to stay moist even when I reheated them to use for another meal.   My chicken breast often dries out but from now on I will brine beforehand!  I didn’t end up using the brown sugar but did use the recommended spices for a delicious savory chicken breast!  Super moist!  Thank you Budget Bytes!
Doubled the recipe and meal prepped this tonight.
Thank you!  I actually use this with a pork loin I cut down in slices and tell my kids are pork chops.  They love them and have taken camping as well!
This is my kids favorite chicken recipe.  So good:)
Mind blown!  I never want to make chicken any other way again! 😍

Winner Winner delicious chicken dinner. I dislike chicken breast. Never ever eat it. There was a huge sale on it $3.99/lb boneless skinless so I got a huge package. I did the brine as directed, all the spices and WOW so delicious. The brine is a magic secret for sure.

We always brine our chicken breasts! 
I've found that I can make the brine recipe as stated and divide it in half.
Then add more plain water to cover my chicken in whatever dish I intend to store them in.  I keep the unused half in the fridge for use the following week.
